content.text:
The drawing shows a thiophene ring: a five-membered ring with one sulfur and four carbons.

- The sulfur is at the bottom left.
- The carbon bearing Cl (C2) is bonded to sulfur.
- The carbon bearing NO2 (C3) is next to C2.
- The remaining ring carbons are C4 and C5, with C5 bonded to sulfur.

The double bonds are C2=C3 (the inner line drawn between the Cl carbon and the NO2 carbon) and C4=C5 (the double line on the left side).

Writing the ring as SMILES: S1C(Cl)=C([N+](=O)[O-])C=C1. This gives 2-chloro-3-nitrothiophene, with the ring closing back to sulfur.

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)c1ccsc1Cl
